sources.researchNote: The caption settles the identification: it presents him as “a fellow songwriter” beside Hoagy Carmichael, which fits the lyricist of the Broadway and Hollywood years and not a namesake, and it places him in the Californian desert resort where he lived out his later life. The occasion is a bar opening, not a professional gathering, and the picture is the only likeness of him gathered here; it stands twenty-seven years after the song of his that enters the Kaper record.

media.title: Sidney Clare with Hoagy Carmichael at the Beachcomber — Desert Sun, 1956
media.description: Press photograph from the opening night of the Beachcomber in Palm Springs, published in the Desert Sun on 13 October 1956: Sidney Clare at the left, Hoagy Carmichael in the centre and Arthur Gordon of Fleischmann Distilleries at the right. The printed caption is reproduced beneath the picture.
media.altText: Three men in suits standing in conversation at a bar opening, with the newspaper caption printed beneath.
media.rightsNote: Reuse rights are not cleared. The picture is credited to the newspaper itself, and a United States issue of 1956 kept its copyright only if the registration was renewed after twenty-eight years; the inventory of first periodical renewals kept at the University of Pennsylvania has no entry for this title, which records no renewal but does not prove that none was made. The digitising library states no rights position of its own. The local 331 × 238 pixel reproduction is therefore used for the identification of the sitter alone, with the newspaper, the holding collection and the unresolved renewal stated alongside it.
